connections.why: Enzymes are proteins whose structure follows from biological molecules
Phospholipids and proteins build the cell membrane
Organelles are defined and compartmentalised by membranes
DNA must be replicated before a cell divides by mitosis
Genes code for the enzymes that catalyse metabolism
Gas exchange depends on diffusion across membranes
Cell features are used to classify and relate organisms
Transport systems carry the gases exchanged at surfaces
Respiration is a controlled enzyme-catalysed pathway
Photosynthesis enzymes fix carbon in the Calvin cycle
Respiration regenerates the ATP cells spend on work
The light reactions produce ATP for carbon fixation
Photosynthesis fixes the energy that flows through ecosystems
Human activity disrupts populations and nutrient cycles
Selective reabsorption in the kidney relies on transport across membranes
Hormonal and nervous control coordinate homeostasis
Meiosis produces the gametes used in sexual reproduction
Fusion of gametes determines the inheritance of alleles
Inherited variation is the substrate for natural selection
Gene technology manipulates DNA understood at the molecular level
Selection over time generates the biodiversity that is classified
